# Northwest Bail Bonds: expanded site summary

## What the company does

Northwest Bail Bonds provides commercial Bail Bond assistance from Billings throughout Montana. A caller can begin with the arrested person's full name and the jail or county. The Bond amount and a callback number are helpful when available. The direct line is (406) 601-1225 and is answered 24/7. Email inquiries can be sent to northwestbailbond@gmail.com; the website prepares a draft in the visitor's own email app and does not submit the form to a website database.

## Customer-service position

Northwest Bail Bonds is built around customer service. Urgent service can still be personal. A useful call should leave a family better informed, more grounded, and clear about the next decision. The website encourages callers to ask about the complete fee, collateral, payment timing, signer obligations, court responsibilities, and license verification before signing.

## Montana coverage

Northwest serves all 56 Montana counties. The service-area page contains an interactive map built from U.S. Census cartographic county boundaries. A user can search for a county or select its actual shape on the map; the chosen county is then highlighted. Billings is the company home base, and the map does not claim that Northwest has an office in every county.

## Bail Bond process overview

1. Confirm the arrested person's name and custody location.
2. Review the available bond information and written agreement.
3. Ask about fees, collateral, payment dates, and all signer responsibilities.
4. If the customer chooses to proceed, complete the required documents.
5. The agent coordinates with the appropriate detention facility. Release timing remains under the control of the court and facility.

## Licensing and legal information

Montana insurance producer licensing information is available from the Montana Commissioner of Securities and Insurance at https://csimt.gov/insurance/licensing/. Court information is available from the Montana Judicial Branch at https://courts.mt.gov/. Legal strategy and advice should come from a qualified attorney. The State Bar of Montana provides public attorney information at https://www.montanabar.org/For-the-Public/Hiring-an-Attorney-in-Montana.

## Frequently asked questions

### What information should a caller have?
The person's full name, county or detention facility, bond amount if known, and callback number are enough to start. Call even when some details are missing.

### How much does a Montana Bail Bond cost?
The exact fee and possible collateral depend on the Bond and circumstances. Ask for the complete written terms and responsibilities before signing.

### How long does release take?
Timing depends on court status, the detention facility, paperwork, staffing, and other conditions. An agent can move promptly but should not promise an exact release time.

### Can Northwest help outside Billings?
Yes. Northwest Bail Bonds serves all 56 Montana counties from its Billings home base.

### Is the line available at night, on weekends, or on holidays?
Yes. The direct phone line is available 24 hours a day, seven days a week.

## Our story

Northwest Bail Bonds began in Billings after seeing how cold and confusing the Bail process can feel from the other side. The company grew through real relationships across Montana. Its work includes answering the phone, being straight about the Bond at hand, and helping people take care of what comes next. When circumstances allow, that has included a ride home, transportation to court, or help finding the next opportunity. Northwest believes one bad night does not have to become a person's whole story.

## Joel Graf — A Bond Beyond Bail

Northwest Bail Bonds grew from Joel Graf's own experience with second chances, faith, and service. His path included wrestling, healthcare, roofing work in Crow, and law enforcement in Hardin before he built a Bail Bond company focused on helping people through difficult moments. The full founder story, including the personal losses and community commitments that shaped the company, is published on /about#joel-story.

## Source-backed Montana facts

- Montana has 56 counties; the site uses official administrative and U.S. Census cartographic boundaries.
- Montana courts may use a validated pretrial assessment, but the Montana Judicial Branch states that the recommendation does not replace a judge's discretion.
- MCA 33-26-109 requires fees or interest beyond the minimum Surety Bail Bond premium to be disclosed when the contract is executed and acknowledged by all parties.
- Montana Judicial Branch materials describe a presumptive right to release on Bail before conviction, subject to stated exceptions and reasonable safety conditions.
